This is one dissent recorded in a manifesto about sustaining human knowledge in the age of AI. Which fault line does it fall on?

Options:
- consent_or_payment: consent and payment mechanism: opt-in / levies / dues on existing text vs open training, pay at output, contracts for new work (Salib, Bratton, O'Reilly against the majority)
- model_in_loop: whether a model belongs in the checking loop or the room at all (Becker, Turkle)
- other: anything else

Text:

Only epistemic trust earned with warrants licenses trust in scientific uses, and human roles in the loop must be epistemically justified, not kept by default.
raw: {"choice":"other","why":"The dissent concerns epistemic warrant: \"human roles in the loop must be epistemically justified, not kept by default.\" It questions keeping humans in the loop by default. It does not argue that a model should be excluded from the checking loop or the room, which is the Becker/Turkle line. It also says nothing about consent, levies or payment. It touches the same loop question from the opposite side, but it is best classed as a distinct objection."}

parsed.why: The dissent concerns epistemic warrant: "human roles in the loop must be epistemically justified, not kept by default." It questions keeping humans in the loop by default. It does not argue that a model should be excluded from the checking loop or the room, which is the Becker/Turkle line. It also says nothing about consent, levies or payment. It touches the same loop question from the opposite side, but it is best classed as a distinct objection.
